citation: Customer A MSA security schedule item (3) (MSA-A (3))
trigger: Any suspected security incident that could affect Customer A data or systems, including ransomware on the laptop that holds Customer A programs, credentials, or VPN access
deadline: Within 24 hours of discovery (the runbook targets the first hour)
notify: Customer A production superintendent by phone, then email; copy the Customer A IT and SCADA contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual; the shortest clock in this matrix

obligation: Notice to other customers whose systems the laptop reached
citation: Customers B, C, and D MSA confidentiality clauses; POL-01 10.3
trigger: Ransomware or compromise of the laptop or email account when the laptop connected to, or held programs, gauges, or credentials for, the customer in the last 30 days
deadline: Same day (POL-01 10.3); the MSAs set no fixed time
notify: Customer B operations manager (ask to disable the shared remote login); Customers C and D contacts

obligation: Oil discharge notice to the National Response Center
trigger: Discharge of oil in a quantity that may be harmful (40 CFR 110.3: for example a film or sheen on the water or adjoining shorelines), for example a tank overflow after loss of control at a customer site
deadline: Immediately, as soon as the person in charge of the facility has knowledge
notify: National Response Center (800-424-8802); if not practicable, the Coast Guard or EPA on-scene coordinator
applies_at_this_tier: Only if a release reaches water. The customer, as facility operator, is normally the person in charge; the owner tells the customer at once and calls the NRC only if acting as the person in charge on site and no customer contact can be reached

trigger: Unauthorized access to the helpers' W-9 data (names with Social Security numbers) in the email and file account, the accounting service, or the laptop
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred; delay only on a law enforcement request; a documented no-harm determination is the only alternative

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the business holds personal information of 2 individuals; recheck if that grows

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time

obligation: Provider breach notice to the business (inbound)
trigger: The accounting service or productivity suite provider (third-party agents holding the helpers' data) has a breach of a system it maintains for the business
deadline: Provider must notify the business no later than 10 days after determination; the business then gives the (4) notice
notify: The business (owner-operator), at the business email address
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - watch for provider notices; the provider list marks who holds personal information

trigger: Affected helpers who reside outside Florida
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely - both helpers reside in Florida; recheck at each hire of a helper

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA

obligation: Voluntary report to CISA and the FBI
citation: No legal requirement for this business (see the CIRCIA row); CISA and FBI reporting channels
trigger: Ransomware on the laptop, especially if it reached or threatened a customer's control system
deadline: As soon as practicable; the runbook targets day 0 to 1, coordinated with the affected customers
notify: CISA (cisa.gov/report or 844-729-2472); FBI field office or IC3
applies_at_this_tier: Voluntary - recommended; supports the OFAC mitigating factor and warns other operators

deadline: Per policy (use the carrier's breach hotline before hiring outside firms)
applies_at_this_tier: Not yet - no cyber policy until coverage is bought (due 2026-10-31, MSA-A (8)); general liability does not cover this; ask the agent

obligation: Reporting of actual or threatened cyber incidents at MTSA facilities / OCS facilities / vessels
trigger: Cyber incident involving or endangering a vessel, harbor, port, or waterfront facility
deadline: Immediately (6.16-1); 'without delay' to the National Response Center for entities not reporting under 6.16-1
notify: FBI, CISA (for any cyber incident), and the Coast Guard Captain of the Port; or National Response Center
applies_at_this_tier: No - onshore work only; no vessel, waterfront facility, or OCS facility (N21-R01 not applicable, P03)

trigger: Cybersecurity incident at a TSA-notified pipeline owner or operator
deadline: As soon as practicable, but no later than 72 hours after identifying a cybersecurity incident
notify: CISA Central (cisa.gov/report or 844-729-2472); CISA shares with TSA
applies_at_this_tier: No - the business operates no pipeline and has no TSA notice (N21-R02 not applicable, P03). A TSA-notified customer would report its own incident

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident report / ransom payment report (PROPOSED - not yet in effect)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment by a covered entity
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours after reasonable belief a covered cyber incident occurred; 24 hours after ransom payment disbursed
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; as proposed, the business is far below the $47.0 million SBA standard for NAICS 213112 and meets no sector criterion (P03); recheck when final

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Covered equipment or services identified during performance of a federal contract
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; further report within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the business holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Covered article identified during performance of a federal contract
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further report within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the business holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
